title: Add token chronicle aggregator and proactive alert conductor
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds a token chronicle aggregator service that produces compact per-invocation token rollups and a proactive alert conductor that dampens noisy token-cost/latency alerts by applying adaptive suppression and guided fallback rules.
description: What: Introduces a new token chronicle aggregator that creates compact, time-bucketed per-invocation token rollups (chronicles) and a Proactive Alert Conductor (PAC) that consumes those chronicles to apply dynamic alert suppression, escalation scoring, and automated fallback recommendations. Why: Long-tail token-cost and microburst latency alerts were generating noisy paging and obscuring genuine regressions. Rather than simply coarsening sampling, this PR builds a server-side rollup layer that preserves important signal (phase breakdowns, kv-hydration events) while enabling deterministic alert orchestration. Design: chronicle-aggregator service ingests sampled spans + token-phase annotations and emits per-invocation chronicle keys, a compact delta-encoding of token counts by phase, and an embedding of prompt-shape fingerprint. The PAC subscribes to the chronicle topic and maintains a short-term history per route/tenant to compute an alert score and suppression token using exponential decay and seasonality smoothing. The PAC also produces fallback recommendations (route to cheaper model variant, adjust batching window, or pin KV-cache warmup) via an action API consumed by the routing policy engine. Backwards compatibility: Chronicle records are produced alongside existing spans; no upstream agent changes required. Rollout: 1) deploy aggregator behind a feature flag; 2) enable PAC in read-only mode (record-only) for two days to validate signals; 3) enable suppression with conservative thresholds, then incrementally increase aggressiveness by route. Testing: unit tests for rollup correctness, e2e synthetic replay tests to validate suppression behavior, canary on staging with live traffic. Monitoring: dashboards added for chronicle ingestion latency, chronicle size distribution, PAC suppression ratio, and false-suppression sampler. Security: chronicles are pseudonymized for non-admin teams and respect tenant scoping. Linked work: ENG-8273. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] dashboard panels [x] docs update [x] migration/rollout plan. Commits summary: "init: add chronicle aggregator service and proto schema", "add: chronicle writer and delta-encoder", "add: PAC engine and suppression policy DSL", "test: synthetic replay harness for chronicle->PAC", "infra: topic + RBAC + helm chart updates", "docs: observability/chronicle and PAC guide". Changed areas: server/observability/chronicle_aggregator/*, server/observability/pac/*, infra/helm/observability-charts/*, webapp/dashboards/chronicle-overview.json, tests/observability/replaybench/*, docs/observability/chronicle.md. Review conversation highlights: "Liam Chen: Can we ensure chronicle payload remains <= 2KB for the 99.9th percentile?" "Aisha: yes, delta-encoder + shard-level truncation keeps the payload under 1.6KB in our synthetic worst case; added a unit to enforce size" "Priya Menon: PAC suppression must be explainable to oncall; include action trace and reason codes" "Aisha: added human-readable reason codes and a UI link to the chronicle for each suppression event" "Diego Alvarez: verify no signal loss for phase boundaries when using delta encoding" "Aisha: added a phase-boundary-preserving tag and test coverage" CI summary: build (pass), unit tests (pass), integration replay (pass), lint (pass), e2e-canary (pass). Merge: merged via squash on 2024-11-14 after approvals from all reviewers. Rollout notes: initial rollout to staging on 2024-11-10, read-only PAC observed on 2024-11-12, suppression enabled 2024-11-13 for 10% of traffic, global enable 2024-11-14. Post-merge actions: monitor suppression false-positive rate, iterate suppression thresholds, add model-variant auto-fallback tuning to Redwood Optimize as follow-up.
